title: 3D Finish: option to ignore/fill model features below the surface (land model)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
A 3D Finish over a plate with bolt holes wants, for this part, the opposite of "the finished surface is the model": a land finish over the top that flies over the holes instead of diving down their walls. There is no suppression/fill knob today (`finishing3d/params.rs` has none), and the generator's own law says the dive is by design.

**The part** (mm BREP STEP, 21 KB - a converted SolidWorks bracket plate; happy to attach on request): a 171.45 x 19.05 x 8.89 mm plate, top face genuinely folded (~8.4 mm high near the ends down to ~4.5 mm mid-run). Two bolt-hole stations (x=28.575 and 142.875, y=-9.525): each a Ø3.4 mm through hole with a Ø6.5 mm x ~1.7 mm deep counterbore opening from the **bottom** face. 1048 facets after import. A 3 mm ball-nose run (waterline and parallel).

**What happens.** Both patterns cut the folded top correctly, but the paths also dive into the hole mouths and trail down the hole walls - visible as plunge trails in the section views below, and as the Z-colored ring pileups at the two stations in the top views. Each run additionally reports:

> rings: 4 ring entries refused - their plunge column from the approach plane crosses the solid; what hides there stands as rest, reported not cut

(the four cylindrical surfaces: through-hole walls + counterbores). Inside the bores the material stands as uncut rest, reported but not cut.

The module doc states the governing law: the finished surface is the model itself, and **only outer loops are cut paths** - "Interior-feature waterlines (tool inside a slot or bore) need a reachability test on hole interiors and are deferred - logged in RECOMMENDED.md" (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/mod.rs`). So the tool following hole walls from outside is what the current model promises; what's missing is the land case above.

**Workarounds tried.**
- 2D operation at constant Z: the top face folds 8.4 -> 4.5 mm, so no single Z follows it.
- Fill the holes in the CAD source: works, but re-import friction each revision, and it destroys the hole features the drilling ops need.
- Flush plug bodies over the holes: same friction.

**Wanted.** A 3D Finish option that ignores model features below the surface being finished - a land model. Shaped as a "land Z" / ignore-below-Z parameter (or a per-operation "fill holes below the finish surface" toggle): the forbidden-center region is built only from geometry above the land, so rings and parallel passes cross the hole mouths uninterrupted. The rest report then says what stands as land (suppressed on purpose) instead of the refused-rings note.

Done means: with the option set, waterline and parallel fly over both stations with no wall dives; the refuse note is replaced by an explicit land statement; UI + MCP get the parameter; tests pin the behavior.

**Evidence** (generated straight from the STEP import + the `finishing3d` generators; section plane y=-9.525 through both stations; feed moves colored cyan=high to magenta=low, rapids hidden; section/side views stretched vertically ~4x for legibility - the plate is a 19:1 thin strip at equal aspect). The sections show the plate cut into three chunks with the two through-gaps (note the stepped counterbore notch at the bottom face) and the plunge trails descending into them. No travel is out of model: every feed point sits within the model bbox + the 3 mm tool radius, and the deepest boundary cuts are ball breakouts at plate edges. Of ~40k feed points only a handful drop below z=0.05 and none fall inside the bore radii - every sub-surface point is a ball breakout at a plate edge or corner.
